newsitem.title: USA: Citizens Utilities sued by investors.
newsitem.headline: Citizens Utilities sued by investors.

text.p: A lawsuit has been filed against Citizens Utilities Co, accusing the company and its officers of misrepresenting material information concerning its telecommunications expansion, lawyers for the plaintiffs said Thursday.

In particular, the complaint alleges defendants misrepresented and failed to disclose at all relevant times that the company's entrance into the long-distance telephone market was failing and that it would be forced to scale back its expansion plans and record a $185 million asset writedown, the lawyers said.

Because of the issuance of a series of allegedly false and misleading statements concerning Citizens' business and defendants' concealment of the above matters, the price of Citizens common stock was artificially inflated during the Class Period, the lawyers said.

The plaintiffs also contend that, while such material information was misrepresented or omitted, certain Citizens insiders took the opportunity to sell substantial amounts of Citizens common stock and the company completed a $200 million debenture offering and acquired two companies in stock-for-stock transactions.
The company was not immediately available for comment.

The plaintiffs in the class action lawsuit, which was filed in U.S. District Court in Connecticut, are being represented by the law firm of Milberg Weiss Bershad Hynes & Lerach LLP and Stull, Stull & Brody.
The lawsuit is in behalf of investors who acquired stock between September 5, 1996, and July 11, 1997.
